summary.user-story: As a developer, I want status updates delivered via the existing SSE stream, so that the Telegram bot can receive status without a separate channel.
summary.description: This story extends the existing SSE (Server-Sent Events) streaming protocol to include status frames. Status frames will be interleaved with existing token frames during streaming, allowing the Telegram bot to receive real-time status updates (e.g., "Annie is thinking...", "Calling get_portfolio...") through the same stream used for LLM response tokens.

dependencies.dependency: Story 11.1 - Status Emitter Infrastructure must be complete before implementing this story

criterion.title: Status Frame Type
criterion.requirements: - New SSE frame format: {"type": "status", "message": "..."} - Interleaved with existing token frames during streaming - Maintains frame ordering (status frames appear when emitted) - JSON format consistent with existing token/done/error frames

criterion.title: Stream Route Updates
criterion.requirements: - /api/stream/{conversation_id} endpoint emits status frames - StatusContext initialized at stream start with SSE write callback - Status callback writes formatted SSE event to response stream - Status frames sent immediately (not buffered)

criterion.title: Backward Compatibility

section.name: Existing SSE Frame Formats
section.description: The backend currently uses three SSE frame types for streaming LLM responses. All frames are JSON objects sent as SSE "data:" events.

section.name: Stream Generator Architecture
section.description: The stream_generator() function in stream.py orchestrates SSE streaming. It yields SSE event dictionaries that are automatically formatted by EventSourceResponse. Each event has "event" and "data" fields.
section.code-reference:
@observe(name="llm_streaming", as_type="span") async def stream_generator( conversation_id: str, messages: List[Dict[str, Any]], request: Request, state_manager: Optional[StateManager] = None ) -> AsyncGenerator[Dict[str, Any], None]: """ Generate SSE events from LLM streaming response with tool orchestration.
Handles: - Tool schema fetching from MCP server - Function calling with LLM - Tool execution via MCP client - Multi-step tool calling (max 5 iterations) - Error handling for tool failures - Storing assistant response in Redis after completion
Args: conversation_id: Unique conversation identifier messages: List of chat messages to send to LLM request: FastAPI request object for disconnection detection state_manager: Optional StateManager for storing assistant response
Yields: SSE event dictionaries with type, data, and optional event fields """

section.name: SSE Endpoint
section.description: The /api/stream/{conversation_id} endpoint returns an EventSourceResponse that streams events from stream_generator(). This endpoint is called by the Telegram bot after the chat endpoint creates a conversation.
section.code-reference:
@router.get("/stream/{conversation_id}") @observe(name="stream_request", as_type="trace") async def stream_response(conversation_id: str, request: Request): """ Stream LLM response via Server-Sent Events (SSE).
This endpoint establishes an SSE connection, loads conversation context from Redis, and streams tokens from the LLM in real-time. After streaming completes, stores the assistant's response in conversation history.
Args: conversation_id: Unique conversation identifier request: FastAPI request object
Returns: EventSourceResponse: SSE stream with token events
Raises: HTTPException: 503 if concurrent stream limit exceeded HTTPException: 500 if state management fails
SSE Event Format: Token event: {"type":"token","content":"text chunk"} Completion event: {"type":"done","tokens_used":{"prompt":N,"completion":M}} Error event: {"type":"error","message":"error message","code":"ERROR_CODE"} """

technical-challenge.title: Callback in Generator Pattern
technical-challenge.description: The status callback needs to inject frames into an async generator. The recommended approach is to use an asyncio.Queue that the StatusContext writes to, and the generator periodically drains.

step.title: Define SSE status frame format helper
step.description: Create format_status_frame(message: str) helper function that returns SSE event dict in same format as token frames.

step.title: Initialize StatusContext in stream_generator
step.description: Import StatusContext from backend.api.status and initialize it at the start of stream_generator() with an async queue-based callback.

step.title: Drain status queue before streaming events
step.description: Before yielding each token/done/error event, drain the status queue to ensure status frames are interleaved correctly.

step.title: Emit initial "thinking" status
step.description: Immediately after StatusContext initialization, emit "Annie is thinking..." status before any tool calls or LLM processing begins.

step.title: Add integration tests
step.description: Test status frame emission during stream, interleaving with token frames, multiple status frames in sequence, and backward compatibility.

file.changes: - Add import for StatusContext from backend.api.status - Add format_status_frame() helper function - Initialize StatusContext with async queue callback in stream_generator() - Emit initial "thinking" status - Drain status queue before yielding each event - Handle status queue in both Gemini and OpenAI/Grok streaming paths
- Add test for status frame emission - Add test for status frame interleaving with token frames - Add test for backward compatibility (clients ignoring status frames)

notes.note: This story requires Story 11.1 (Status Emitter Infrastructure) to be complete. The StatusContext class must exist in backend/api/status.py with emit_status() and context manager support.

The stream_generator() function has two distinct code paths: one for Gemini (lines 138-243) and one for OpenAI/Grok (lines 245-617). Status queue draining must be added to both paths to ensure consistent behavior across all LLM providers.

Status frames should be sent immediately (not buffered). The asyncio.Queue pattern ensures that status messages are queued instantly and drained before each event yield, maintaining real-time status updates.
Clients that only parse token/done/error frames will automatically ignore status frames since they check event["type"]. No client changes are required.
